# Categorical Data and Contingency Tables

When your variables are categorical (pass/fail, language, defect type), counts in a table are the data.

## A 2x2 Example

Do tests pass at the same rate under two test-generation tools?

```r
tbl <- matrix(c(82, 18,
                70, 30),
              nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE,
              dimnames = list(tool = c("A", "B"),
                              outcome = c("pass", "fail")))
chisq.test(tbl)
```

For 2x2 tables with small expected counts (any expected < 5), use Fisher's exact test:

```r
fisher.test(tbl)
```

## Larger Contingency Tables

```r
tbl3 <- matrix(c(50, 30, 20,
                 40, 35, 25,
                 30, 40, 30),
               nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE,
               dimnames = list(language = c("Java", "Python", "Rust"),
                               severity = c("low", "med", "high")))
chisq.test(tbl3)
```

## Effect Size: Cramer's V

```r
chi <- chisq.test(tbl3)
n   <- sum(tbl3)
k   <- min(nrow(tbl3), ncol(tbl3))
V   <- sqrt(chi$statistic / (n * (k - 1)))
V
```

Rules of thumb: 0.1 small, 0.3 medium, 0.5 large.

## McNemar's Test for Paired Categorical Data

```r
m <- matrix(c(40, 12,
               5, 43),
            nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
mcnemar.test(m)
```

## Goodness-of-Fit

```r
observed <- c(95, 110, 105, 90, 100)
chisq.test(observed)        # H0: uniform
```
